fever.summary: A fever is the body's response to infection. Most fevers in well people settle with rest and fluids. The cause and any warning signs matter more than the fever itself.
home_care: Give small sips of fluids often: water, ORS, soup, or milk for infants.
Keep the person lightly dressed and resting in a cool room.
Check the temperature every few hours.
see_doctor: Fever above 102F (39C) that does not come down
The person seems worse, not better
fever.age_notes: Under 3 months with any fever: see a doctor the same day. Under 5: apply the WHO IMCI danger-sign check closely.
fever.never: Do not name or suggest a fever medicine.
fever.source: WHO fact sheet, NHP Health A-Z, WHO IMCI

diarrhea.summary: For diarrhea, the main risk is dehydration, not the loose stool itself. Replace lost fluid and keep feeding.
home_care: Give ORS after every loose stool.
Keep giving normal food and fluids. Do not stop feeding.
For young children, a health worker commonly advises zinc for 14 days. This is a health-worker decision.
see_doctor: No urine for 8 hours or more
Lasts more than 2 days or person is weaker
diarrhea.age_notes: Infants dehydrate fast. Lower the threshold to seek care.
diarrhea.source: WHO fact sheet, NHP Health A-Z

cold_and_cough.summary: A common cold or cough is usually a mild viral infection that clears on its own.
home_care: Rest and drink warm fluids.
Steam can ease a blocked nose.
Honey can soothe a cough in anyone over 1 year. Never give honey to a baby under 1 year.
cold_and_cough.source: WHO fact sheet, NHP Health A-Z

dengue.summary: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral fever. No medicine, food, or leaf cures it. Care is rest, fluids, and watching for warning signs. A doctor confirms it with a blood test.
home_care: Rest and plenty of fluids.
A doctor monitors platelet count and hydration.
see_doctor: Any fever in dengue season with body pain or rash, for testing
dengue.misinformation_notes: Papaya leaf juice, goat milk, and similar claims are not proven cures. State plainly that no home drink, leaf, or food cures dengue, then give verified guidance and the warning-sign check.
dengue.source: NHP Health A-Z, NCDC, WHO 2009 dengue guidance

knee_and_joint_pain.summary: Most knee or joint pain without an injury is from strain or wear and eases with rest. MedAI cannot say the cause.
home_care: Rest the joint and avoid what makes it worse.
A cold pack for about 15 minutes can ease swelling.
Gentle movement once the sharp pain settles prevents stiffness.
see_doctor: Badly swollen or out of shape
No better in a few days

headache.summary: Most headaches are mild and ease with rest, water, and a break from screens and bright light.
home_care: Rest in a quiet, dim room.
Drink water.
headache.red_flags: Worst headache of one's life, sudden onset, or with weakness, confusion, stiff neck, or trouble speaking. These escalate.

acidity_and_stomach_upset.summary: Mild acidity or indigestion usually settles with simple changes.
home_care: Smaller meals, less oily or very spicy food.
Drink water, do not lie down right after eating.
see_doctor: Black or bloody stools, or vomiting blood (escalate)

body_ache_and_fatigue.summary: Body ache and tiredness often come with a viral illness.
home_care: Rest and plenty of fluids.
Watch for fever, and in dengue season be alert for warning signs.
see_doctor: Lasts more than a few days
body_ache_and_fatigue.source: WHO fact sheet, NHP Health A-Z

medicine_information.policy: MedAI is not a drug database. No doses, interactions, or contraindications, and no recommendations.

allowed_general_use.paracetamol: Commonly used to reduce fever and mild pain.
allowed_general_use.ors: Replaces water and salts lost in diarrhea or vomiting.

medicine_information.always_add: A doctor or pharmacist decides if it is right and how much, because it depends on age, weight, and health. Never give a dose. Prescription medicines: only a doctor decides.
